name: Sultamicillin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Sultamicillin is an oral prodrug of ampicillin and sulbactam, both cleared by the kidneys. The Singapore product information lowers dosing frequency when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is 30 mL/min or less, following usual ampicillin practice, but gives no specific interval or dialysis guidance. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Singapore product information uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); single threshold ≤30.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 375 to 750 mg orally twice daily (Singapore NDF).
No adjustment stated above CrCl 30 (Singapore NDF).
Severe impairment (CrCl ≤30 mL/min): give doses less often, as is usual for ampicillin; the source gives no specific interval (Singapore NDF). Specialist input on the interval.

hd: No dialysis guidance in the source. Ampicillin and sulbactam are renally cleared; specialist input on timing after dialysis.
crrt: No guidance; oral prodrug rarely appropriate in CRRT settings.
monitoring: Penicillin allergy history; diarrhea (including Clostridioides difficile); kidney function to set dosing frequency.

pediatric.usual_dose: Under 30 kg: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day orally in 2 divided doses. 30 kg or more: adult dose (Singapore NDF).

renal.recommendation: Normal kidney function: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses (under 30 kg).
